Eligio Lee.bio: Eligio Leeis a South Korean former Mattel employee who worked at the company around 2007. He is currently the CEO of CLO Virtual Fashion's China and Hong Kong branch.

Ethan Noranbrock.bio: Ethan"EFORCE"Noranbrockis an American industrial designer who interned at Mattel from June to August 2025 as part of their Innovation and RC teams. Prior to Mattel he interned at Jazwares; he currently is engaged in an internship with Disney Experiences.

Jonathan Bedford.bio: Jonathan Bedfordis a former Hot Wheels designer who was part of the Hot Wheels design team from around the early 2000s to at least 2006. He is currently the owner of Symple Services, a product design and development firm.

Josh Henson.bio: Joshua D. Hensonis a former designer for Hot Wheels who worked with the company from 2004 to 2010. His first design wasReverb, a collaboration withAlec Tam. After leaving Mattel, he worked at another toy company, Spin Master, and also worked for various film companies designing vehicles for various projects as well as a creative collective. He is currently self-employed, running his own company, Joshua Henson, LLC.

Julian Payne.bio: Julian Richard Payneis a British principal designer for Hot Wheels and Matchbox who has been working at Mattel since 1998. Most of his work is with regards to playsets, mainlyColor Shiftersplaysets, with some amount of vehicle design as well. He was a part of the Matchbox design team early on in his career but has since moved back.

Keith Hippely.bio: Keith Alan Hippelyis a former Mattel employee who worked with Hot Wheels as a staff designer from 1980 to 2013. He is most noted for having worked on theAttack PackandRoad Beastslines of monster trucks and having developed theSuper SlammersandColor Racersline in the 1980s. He currently works at InvenToy, a company started by him and fellow ex-Hot Wheels engineerEric Ostendorff.

Kevin Gray.bio: Kevin Winfield Grayis a former Mattel employee and programmer who worked with the company from 1985 to 2009. His official role at Mattel was as both a product designer and as a product developer, developing numerous products and redesigning numerous others. He currently runs his own company, General Anomaly Design LLC.

Kurnia Alim.bio: Kurnia Alimis an industrial designer who has been working with Mattel since at least 2012. He has worked on various tracks and playsets and is the current lead designer of theHot Wheels Monster Trucksline, taking over fromBrendon Vetuskey. Prior to working at Mattel he worked at Jakks Pacific.

Leeway Chang.bio: Leeway Changis a Hot Wheels staff designer specializing in graphics design who has worked at Mattel since 2007.

Leon Kosciak.bio: Leon Kosciakis a Polish-American automotive designer who interned at Mattel from June to August 2025. Prior to working at Mattel he interned at a number of automotive design firms and worked as a graphic designer at other firms. He studied at the College for Creative Studies and ArtCenter.

Lindsey Lee.bio: Lindsey Eun-ji Leeis a Korean Hot Wheels designer who worked with Mattel from 2016 to 2022; she is notable as being Hot Wheels's first full-time female designer. This was her first job after graduating from the Art Center College of Design in 2015; prior to that, she interned at the Nissan Headquarter Studios in Tokyo. At Mattel she designed mainly formainline,Premiumand Extensions, as well as being in charge of designing retools for existing castings. After Hot Wheels she relocated back to South Korea and works in the fashion industry, acting as a design lead for the New Era Cap Company.

Ludovico Ferro.bio: Ludovico Ferrois a designer who interned at Hot Wheels in 2005. The only car he designed wasBlastous, a Torpedoes car that came out in the2005 First Editions. In addition to his experience as an intern at Hot Wheels, Ferro also interned for Little Tikes and worked for competing brand Spin Master. He is currently an architect at FK Architects based in Florida.

Manson Cheung.bio: Manson Leo Cheungis a Hot Wheels 3D Modeler who has been working withMattelsince 2000. He is best known for his sculpting work (translating a designer's ideas and drawings into a three-dimensional prototype), but also designs and sculpts his own castings on occasion, usually from movies and the like. He is known on the Internet under his handle "awildermode", and is a well-known DeLorean enthusiast.

Marc Reisen.bio: Marc A. Reisenis an American industrial designer who was one of the six designers who participated in theHot Wheels Designers Challenge; he represented theDodgedivision ofFiat Chrysler Automobiles(now part ofStellantis), for he was Creative Automotive Designer, by designing theDodge XP-07for said series. Reisen joined FCA in 2006 and left in 2008; he has since gone on to a wide variety of companies since then. He is currently Head of Design at Matter, a social media platform for giving and receiving feedback, where he has been since 2018.

Marcel Santos.bio: Marcel Santosis a former Hot Wheels designer who worked with the company from 2016 to 2017. Santos mainly worked on theHot Wheels Cityline of playsets as well as some vehicle work. The Super Ultimate Garage won Toy Of The Year in the Playsets category in 2018. He is currently an Industrial Designer at Walt Disney Imagineering.

Mario Godoy.bio: Mario Enrique Godoyis an American Mattel employee who has been working with Hot Wheels since 2015. He specializes in graphic design, designing graphics for the mainline,Monster Trucksand others. Since 2024 he has been designing Monster Truck bodies, with his first design beingSkelesaurus.

Mark Barthold.bio: Mark John Bartholdis a former Mattel employee who worked at Mattel from 1990 to 2014. He designed for Hot Wheels around the 1990s and 2000s; he was involved with theMotorized X-V Racersseries of cars. He currently works as a Principal Designer for competing brand Spin Master, and owns his own design company, Inventor 8.

Matt Gabe.bio: Matthew Wayne Gabeis a Hot Wheels designer who worked at Mattel from 2009 to 2014 and again since 2018. He specializes in graphic design, with his current role being a lead package designer for Mattel. Prior to working at Mattel, he worked for competing brands Hasbro and Fisher-Price, mainly also as package designer.

Mauricio Bedolla.bio: Mauricio Bedolla Gascais a Mexican former employee of Mattel worked at Mattel from 2005 to 2012. He was also a former Matchbox manager. He currently works as a Design Manager for Lego.

Michael Kollins.bio: Michael Lewis Kollinsis a Hot Wheels designer who worked at Mattel from 1985 to 2004. He is currently an assistant chair at the Otis College of Art and Design, where he has worked since 2005. His last known position was as the Manager of the Collector and Racing lineups; he was responsible for thePro Circuitand thePro Racingseries, as well as the newly-tooled castings in the latter.

Miguel López.bio: Miguel Angel López Jr.is a Spanish-American Hot Wheels designer who worked at Mattel from 2012 to 2015, designing cars for both the Hot Wheels andMatchboxlines. He designed Hot Wheels cars such as theFast 4WDandX-Steam, as well as a number of Star Wars and Disney Character Cars. He is currently a freelance artist, having been one since leaving Mattel, with his notable works now being a number of vehicles for thePaw Patrolline of toys manufactured by competing brand Spin Master. In addition to his work as an artist, López also worked as an English teacher from 2015 to 2017, first in Madrid, Spain and then later in Tokyo, Japan. He is currently based in Japan.

Mike Finizza.bio: Michael Theodore Finizzais aHot Wheelsdesigner who has worked withMattelfrom2002to 2020. Prior to his work at Mattel, he was originally an intern creating "feature dolls" for the Barbie line of products. He is currently employed by competing brand Spin Master as a Staff Designer.

Mike Nuttall.bio: Michael Wayne Nuttallis a former Hot Wheels designer who worked at Mattel's Hot Wheels division from 1999 to 2016; he mostly worked on designing track and playsets but occasionally designed vehicles, with his development on track sets leading him to be dubbed "Track Master Mike". He is decribed as "a master of toy design", he is stated to be able to whip out a "great concept sketch" faster than most people can pick up their pen. He is currently a member of InvenToy, a company started by former Hot Wheels engineersEric OstendorffandKeith Hippely. Prior to his stint at Hot Wheels, he worked for Mattel's Preschool division from 1970 to 1978 before moving to competing brand Tomy.

Nathan Proch.bio: Nathan Clifford Prochis a former designer for Hot Wheels who worked at Mattel from 1993 to 2006; around that time he became debilitated with an unspecified illness which prevented him from working full time, and left soon after. Before his illness, Proch was responsible for the creation of theCM5wheel and the cut-out logos that appeared on the bases of Hot Wheels cars from 2005 to 2006. He also acted as Director of Hot Wheels Design for a time. Proch was inducted into the Diecast Hall of Fame in 2014 but declined the award; he has since kept a low profile.

Omar González.bio: Omar Rene Gonzálezis an industrial designer who has been working with Mattel since 2023. He is currently part of the Track and Playsets team and is responsible for the design of theHot Wheels Monster Trucks Big RigsfollowingBrendon Vetuskey's early concepts. Prior to working at Mattel he worked at Jazwares, Strottman International and various other companies.

Omar Rehman.bio: Omar Nayeemur Rehmanis a former Hot Wheels designer who interned at Mattel from June to December 2017. He designed both vehicles and smaller playsets. Prior to working at Mattel, Rehman interned at The Carlab and was PR for EuroJet Racing; after his stint at Hot Wheels he interned at NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory and worked as an industrial designer on contract with studio.VO and MODUS Group. He was last a communication designer for D-Ford, the Ford Motor Company's human-centric design group. He can be found on the internet under the handle @youknowitsomar.

Otto Kuhni.bio: Otto Johnson Kuhniwas a graphic artist that designed many the early art work for blisterpacks, cases and sets. Born in 1927 in Utah the fourth of five children, Kuhni began work as a freelance artist in 1962 and began work with Mattel in 1967 after being hired byRick Irons, doing many of the drawings for card art and playsets; he even designed some large playsets himself. Kuhni retired in 1995, but returned part-time to do artwork for the then-newHot Wheels Collectorsseries of cars, the accompanyingRed Line Cluband various other retro-themed products. Kuhni died in 2017, aged 90; his legacy lives in the form of his artwork as well as theCustom Otto, a rendition of the generic car he drew for the 1968 packaging artwork that was ultimately never released in the line and named in his honor.

Paul DeLorean.bio: Paul Joseph DeLoreanis a Hot Wheels designer who worked at Mattel from 2011 to 2013. The nephew ofJohn DeLorean, he designed 10-15 Hot Wheels vehicles. He is currently the owner and CEO of DeLorean Aerospace LLC. DeLorean rejoined Mattel in 2023 on a temporary basis and again in 2025 on a full-time basis.

Paul Norris.bio: Paul Norrisis a former Hot Wheels designer who worked with Mattel from 1982 to the 1990s. Norris mainly worked on playsets during his tenure at Hot Wheels but designed theSplittin' Image IIalongsideBruce Baurand worked on theMechanixline.

Peter Chuang.bio: Peter Chuangis a Mattel employee who has been working with Mattel since1999. He is currently a design manager for theCarsandMatchboxranges, formerly being a designer on Mattel's card games and certain entertainment properties.

Phil Riehlman.bio: Philip Oscar Riehlmanis a Hot Wheels designer that has been designing Hot Wheels cars since 1993. His first designs were theTwin Mill IIand theSilhouette IIas collaborations withBruce Baur; he also designed briefly for sister line Matchbox and currently also serves as a senior manager of Mattel. He was lead designer for theHot Wheels idline prior to its cancelation and currently designs models for Premium and the mainline; he is the lead designer forPremium 1:43andElite 64. He initially worked as an intern in 1991 before applying for a permanent position at the Male Action Figures department in 1993; he was subsequently transferred back to the Hot Wheels department, where he has been ever since.

Raffy Gonzalez.bio: Raffy A. Gonzalezis a former Hot Wheels designer who interned at Mattel in 2003 and worked there from 2005 to 2007. Gonzalez interned at Mattel in 2003 and was noted as being one of the first interns to be "allowed" to design a car. After his internship, Gonzalez returned to Mattel in 2005 as a "freelance design vendor" and left in 2007; he then worked for Lance Powersports, a manufacturer of electric scooters. He is currently a design chief at Revision Design Studio.

Rick Jung.bio: Rick Jungis a formerHot Wheelsdesigner who interned forMattelfor seven months from June to December of2017who went on to work for Mazda North America. He currently works for Jacques Marie Mage and designs eyewear and eye protection.

Rob Matthes.bio: Robert William Matthesis a designer who worked at Hot Wheels from 2002 to 2017 and again since2023. He served as a design manager for Hot Wheels from 2008 to 2017, managing the $1 lineup from 2008 to2012as well as being the design lead for theHot Wheels Eliteand 1:50 scale lines and then managed the playset team until his departure in 2017. He also manages his own company, SpeedShift Art, specializing in automotive illustration. He rejoined Hot Wheels in 2023, working mainly onPremiumproducts and currently manages theFormula One CollectionandRacing Culturelines.

Robert Heath.bio: Robert Heathis a designer who worked at Hot Wheels from2013to2020known for his work onSplash RidesandCharacter Cars. Prior to his work at Mattel, he was a designer at competing brand Spin Master and at Disney Consumer Products. He is currently managing his own design firm, Pencil Dog Creations.

Sam Brown.bio: Samuel Brownis a former designer who interned at Hot Wheels in 2004. After his internship at Hot Wheels, he moved to Adidas; he currently works at Riot Games as a concept artist, where he has worked since 2021. Prior to his move to Riot Games he worked at 343 Industries, also as a concept artist.

Scott Robertson.bio: Scott Robertsonis a designer who designed cars for Hot Wheels in 2005; he did not actually work for Mattel during that time however. Robertson is an educator on the side, teaching initially at the Art Center College of Design from 1995 to 2010 and then from his own company, Scott Robertson Design LLC. He authored the bookHow To Draw Cars The Hot Wheels Waywith assistance from the Hot Wheels design team.

Sei Cho.bio: Sei Chois a former Hot Wheels designer who worked with Mattel from 2004 to 2006. Originally working with Jada Toys, he left the company in 2004 to join Mattel, where he worked for two years; while at Hot Wheels, Sei worked at the Hot Wheels "Trend" Group alongsideJun Imaito design "unconventional body styles" for Hot Wheels models, such as the Drop Tops and Blings models, stating that "essential line" vehicles (i.e. Realistix) were "a special treat". He also worked onDropstars,Dropstars Urban Assault Vehicles,Custom Classics,Hot Import NightsandHIN D-Forcemodels. After leaving Mattel in 2006, he worked with a number of industrial design firms before he rejoined Jada Toys in 2016, where he currently serves as a design manager.

Shawn Moghadam.bio: Shawn Salimi Moghadam(read "mog-hah-dam") is an industrial designer who worked at Mattel from 2023 to 2024 on a contract. Prior to working at Mattel he worked at Tesla as a visual artist. He also teaches part-time at the Gnomon School of Visual Effects.

Sonny Fisher.bio: Sonny Paul Fisheris a Zambian formerHot Wheelsdesigner who worked atMattelfrom 2020 to 2022. Prior to working at Mattel, Fisher was a designer for the Piaggio Group on a part-time basis and a visual developmental artist at DreamWorks, doing work for theFast & Furious: Spy RacersTV series. He can be found on his website, Fisher Envision. He currently works for Polaris Inc.

Steve Crijns.bio: Steven Crijnsis a Belgian automotive designer who was one of the six designers who participated in theHot Wheels Designers Challenge; he representedLotus Cars, for he was Lead Designer of Lotus, by designing theLotus Conceptfor said series. He first joined Lotus in 1994 and left in 2014 to move to McLaren, where he has remained since. He has worked on the765LT,Speedtailand "a next-generationP1".

Steve Moran.bio: Steven M. Moranis a former Hot Wheels designer who worked at the company from 1997 to 2011. Moran was first asked to direct the Hong Kong Hot Wheels design team in 1997, and became a senior design manager in 2000. He worked with Hot Wheels mainly managing the direction of the Hot Wheels Elite line among other lines and left the design team in 2008 to work for another division of Mattel. Moran left Mattel entirely in 2011 and went to work for Jada Toys; he also founded Moran Devices LLC the same year. Moran returned to Mattel as a "mentor project lead" in 2012 and left in 2015.

Steve Platt.bio: Steven Michael Plattis a designer and modelmaker who worked atMattelfrom roughly1999until sometime around2001after landing his position due to a conversation with his neighbor. Platt collaborated withDave Martisto design the castingSteel Flamedepicting his custom 1999 GMC Sonoma build and was one of the youngest in the design center.

Terry Choy.bio: Terence Allan Choywas a Chinese-American toy designer who designed for Mattel from1984to 2005. He started as Senior Designer (1984-1985), Project Designer (1985-1987), then Senior Project Designer (1988-2005). He was the Project Manager for the Adult/Collector Division of Hot Wheels Racing, which included Formula 1, NASCAR and Rally products. He was responsible for the earliest Batmobile casting designs for Hot Wheels with the 100% Batmobiles Series which debuted in 2003 with the Dream Halloween 1989 Batmobile; made for charity. He was a designer forThe Simpsonstoy line in addition to his Hot Wheels portfolio. He was one of the designers for some of the vehicles for an ill-fatedHe Manmovie, alongside a number of other Hot Wheels designers. Terry passed away on 7 April 2020 from cancer, aged 67.

Thomas Kim.bio: Thomas Yeong-hoon Kimis a Korean-American Mattel employee who has worked with Hot Wheels since 2025 as a casting designer. Prior to working at Mattel he worked at Nissan and General Motors as an automotive designer and held internship opportunities with Bertone and GAEI.

Todd Gibbs.bio: Todd Gibbsis a designer who worked at Mattel from 2012 to 2015. He designed many ofThe Muppets Character Carsand theTarmac Attack. He currently works at Warner Bros.

Tony Martino.bio: Anthony M. Martinois a Hot Wheels designer who worked for Mattel from around 2006 to about 2015. He mainly worked onMonster Jamproducts and designed some playsets.

Vaughan Ling.bio: Vaughan Lingis a former Hot Wheels designer who worked at Mattel in 2011. He was the lead designer for the 2012DC Character Carsline, and assisted with the 3D production ofSuperman. Vaughan has since worked at various animation studios and manages his websiteheavypoly.

Vince Christman.bio: Vincent Christmanis a designer who interned at Hot Wheels from 2011 to 2012. He designed a few trucks from theTrackin' Trucksline includingBone BlazersandCopter Chase. He also designed theYellow Ranger - Tiger ZordCharacter Car. He currently works as an exterior designer for Scout Motors.

Wayne Scott.bio: Wayne Arthur Scott Jr.was a Hot Wheels designer who worked for Mattel from 1997 to 2009. He was mainly a graphic designer, with his name appearing on numerous castings as a sponsor decal; in addition to graphics, Scott also designed castings but not in large volumes. Prior to his stint at Mattel, Scott did graphics for Revell's NASCAR model kits. He passed away on 26 March 2017, aged 45; a cause of death was not announced.

York Bleyer.bio: York H. Bleyeris a former Hot Wheels designer and design manager who worked at Mattel from 2007 to 2011. Prior to working at Mattel, he was an industrial designer, working with numerous companies before moving to Mattel in 2007. Initially working with Tyco, York moved to Hot Wheels in 2011 where he managed various employees and led the Innovation Small Vehicles and Track and Playsets team, in addition to contributing to some design work. Projects he contributed to during his tenure at Hot Wheels includeStealth Rides,Wall Tracks, Batman, Cars, Toy Story, Green Lantern,Speed Racerand Max Steel playsets. After his tenure at Mattel he worked for Ridemakerz and ran his own design studio, and was last an adjunct professor at the Academy of Art University. Driving through the streets of San Francisco provided its challenges but confirmed his belief that a motorcycle was the perfect tool for commuting in the city. He has used this form of transportation for commuting to work in New York City, Detroit and Troy Michigan to the greater Los Angeles Southern California area. Riding bikes has remained his favorite way to travel to this day.
